headline: Tuesday night's rain is now inside the 72-hour window: GFS and RRFS put a short burst around 1 to 4 AM Wednesday, near the 7.1 ft high tide, but the consensus stays well below flooding amounts; the Coastal Flood Warning starts 6 AM Monday.

summary.text: Tuesday night is now in range: GFS 0.49 in and RRFS 0.26 in for their wettest 3 hours, both 1 to 4 AM Wednesday. Consensus up from 0.04 to 0.11 in.
Wettest 3 hours, next 72 h: GFS 0.49, RRFS 0.26, ECMWF 0.14, NBM 0.11, HRRR 0.00 in (HRRR ends Monday night). GFS is the wet outlier, carried by one 0.34 in hour at 3 AM Wednesday.
No street flooding expected on the consensus (0.11 in). Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour; GFS's 0.34 in hour is the closest any model gets.
Showers end today; Monday dry. Steady light rain starts about 5 to 7 PM Tuesday, heaviest overnight into early Wednesday, tapering Wednesday. NWS says timing could slip about 6 hours later.
Tides running about 1.5 ft above prediction. The burst lines up with the 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM Wednesday, so drainage will be slower than on a low tide. Channel low: 0.16 ft at Alameda.
Use dry Monday: clear street drain grates and yard drains, check sandbags, and plan where cars go Tuesday night. Keep the page open Tuesday evening.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Last night's cold front brought only light rain and is slowly leaving the region this morning; NWS San Francisco (3:56 AM) keeps a few showers in the forecast today, drying out this evening, with a brief ridge giving a dry Monday. An upper low then approaches the West Coast, with a shortwave trough bringing rain and wind Tuesday into Wednesday. NWS calls this storm uncertain: the models have struggled, the rain could arrive about 6 hours later than forecast, and amounts might be underdone if a subtropical moisture tap develops (precipitable water near 1.0 in, around the 90th percentile). Gusts mostly 20 to 30 mph. Drying late Wednesday into a dry Thanksgiving and Friday, then more rain possible late Friday into the weekend. Separately, NWS expects major to extreme coastal flooding all week from king tides, surge and warm El Niño waters.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since Saturday afternoon's discussion the 72-hour window has moved forward to early Wednesday, so the first part of the Tuesday storm is now in the data. Wettest 3 hours / total, 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM Wednesday:
• GFS: 0.49 / 0.55 in, wettest 1 to 4 AM Wednesday, with 0.11 in at 1 AM and 0.34 in at 3 AM. Last time it was dry through Tuesday evening. It keeps raining after the window (0.21 in at 4 AM Wednesday), so its wettest 3 hours could end up a little higher.
• RRFS (10 PM Sat run, ends 10 AM Wed): 0.26 / 0.43 in, light rain from 7 PM Tuesday and a 0.19 in hour at 2 AM Wednesday.
• ECMWF: 0.14 / 0.39 in, steady light rain from about 5 PM Tuesday, wettest 8 to 11 PM Tuesday. Its Tuesday total is 0.27 in, close to yesterday's 0.30 in.
• NBM: 0.11 / 0.32 in, light rain from 5 PM Tuesday, wettest 11 PM Tuesday to 2 AM Wednesday. Its Tuesday total fell from 0.42 to 0.18 in, with more of the rain shifted into Wednesday (0.30 in).
• HRRR (2 AM Sun run): 0.00 in. It ends at 10 PM Monday, so it says nothing yet about Tuesday; its 15-minute output is dry through Monday night.

Consensus (HRRR 0.00 × 1.25, RRFS 0.26, NBM 0.11): 0.11 in, up from 0.04 in. That number is probably on the low side because HRRR doesn't reach the storm; the middle of RRFS, ECMWF and NBM would be 0.14 in. Even the wettest model (GFS 0.49 in) stays under the 0.71 in Yellow threshold, but its 0.34 in hour is close to the 0.40 in one-hour burst that raises the rating to Yellow, and HRRR-type guidance has under-forecast local bursts by about 3× before. GFS and RRFS agreeing on a burst around 2 to 3 AM Wednesday is the signal to watch.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model runs about 1.5 ft above the predicted tides at Redwood City, up slightly from 0.9 to 1.4 ft yesterday. This morning's 8.8 ft high at 9:42 AM runs about 10.3 ft; tonight's 6.9 ft high at 11:18 PM about 8.4 ft; Monday's 9.2 ft high at 10:20 AM about 10.7 ft. The model ends at 1 AM Tuesday, so Tuesday and Wednesday are predictions only: 9.5 ft at 11:02 AM Tuesday, a -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM Tuesday (good drainage as the rain starts), 7.1 ft at 1:12 AM Wednesday, and 9.5 ft at 11:46 AM Wednesday. The forecast burst around 1 to 4 AM Wednesday falls right around that 7.1 ft high, which with surge slows the channel. By Wednesday's late-morning king tide the models have the rain mostly light.

NWS coastal products are unchanged: Coastal Flood Advisory until 6 AM Monday, then a Coastal Flood Warning (up to 2.8 ft of inundation in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways) through 4 PM Thursday. San Francisco high tides 2.0 ft above normal this morning, 2.2 Monday, 2.6 Tuesday, 2.8 Wednesday and 2.4 Thursday, including up to 1.6 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas it reads 0.16 ft at 4 AM, with a small bump to 0.21 ft at midnight from last night's rain (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). The gauge upstream of Caltrain last reported 0.07 ft at 5:13 PM Saturday (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft), about 11 hours ago.

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: The front's light rain reached the area last evening: the Caltrain rain gauge's last report, at 9:55 PM Saturday, showed 0.04 in. The Alameda channel gauge barely moved. NWS reports clearing behind the front with patchy valley fog this morning and a few lingering showers today.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low through Monday: no model has meaningful rain. Moderate for Tuesday night: all four models that reach it bring rain, but the wettest 3 hours range from 0.11 to 0.49 in, and the burst depends on whether a convective band forms (GFS, RRFS) or the rain stays steady and light (ECMWF, NBM). NWS flags a possible 6-hour delay, which would move the heaviest rain later Wednesday morning, closer to the 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM, and possible extra moisture that could raise amounts. HRRR will start covering Tuesday later today.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Nothing needed today; showers are light.
• Monday (dry, before the warning-level tides and Tuesday's rain): clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains, check sandbags, and decide where cars will go Tuesday night if the burst holds. Power outages from Tuesday's wind can slow the pumps.
• Tuesday evening: keep this page open; if a burst develops, timestamped photos at the peak help.
• Stay away from the Bay shore and tidal sloughs at the morning high tides; don't walk or drive through moving water.
